_readme: Level 2's townspeople (T32): the same format as Levels/Level_01/plaza_life.json, read by PlazaLifeContent while Office_Level2 is played.
Each talk is optional, replayable local colour: never a clue the case needs, an item, coins, trust or progress. Talks rotate each time.
Where they stand and walk: Levels/Level_02/town_life.json. Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored by the game.

npcs.name: Mang Ernesto
npcs.role: Retired bookkeeper of the market cooperative
npcs.background: Kept the market co-op's books for thirty years; now reads the paper on the plaza bench every afternoon.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Thirty years I kept the market co-op's books. My rule: every peso gets a paper.

lines.speaker: Player
lines.text: And a peso without a paper?

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Is just a story. Nice to hear, hard to check.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: You're helping Rosa from the laundry stall? Good woman. Never late with her stall fees.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: She keeps her daily list in one notebook and the big jobs on separate slips. Old habit from her husband.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Borrowed money spends just like earned money. Until the lender comes back for it.

lines.speaker: Player
lines.text: Wise words.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Expensive words. I learned them the hard way.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Quiet plaza today. Everyone's at the fiesta rehearsal. Suits me fine.

npcs.name: Tess
npcs.background: Runs a small snack cart with her husband; does the family errands round the plaza while her son is at school.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Bread, school glue, a new ledger for our snack cart... I always forget one thing.

lines.speaker: Player
lines.text: Write a list?

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: I did. I forgot the list.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: My husband says receipts are clutter. I say they're how we know the cart is worth the trouble.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Rosa washed my son's school uniforms in one afternoon. Spotless! I don't know how she does it.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: If you see her, tell her the blue shirt finally fits him.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: The tax office helped my mother with her pension papers last year. Very patient people.

lines.speaker: Player
lines.text: Glad to hear it.

npcs.name: Arthur
npcs.background: A familiar consultant taking a slow walk through Coast Tales between appointments.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: A good case starts with listening. The papers make more sense after you know the person.

lines.speaker: Player
lines.text: I'll keep that in mind.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Good. Rosa's been patient with us.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: I take this loop when I need to think. The plaza has a way of clearing the head.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Every person keeps records a little differently. Our job is to understand them, not judge the handwriting.

npcs.name: Mang Dante
npcs.background: A familiar guard making his regular check around the office and plaza.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: All clear around the plaza. I like to check in with everyone on my rounds.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: The office stays busy. Good thing the people here look out for one another.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: If I'm walking, I'm working. If I'm standing still, I'm probably listening.

npcs.name: Marie
npcs.background: Marie is visiting Coast Tales and catching up with the people she knows in the plaza.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Mang Ernesto has a story for every old ledger in town.

lines.speaker: Player
lines.text: I think he enjoys telling them.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: He does. And I enjoy hearing them.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: It's nice to see the plaza feeling busy again. Rosa always brings people together.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: I promised I'd stop by for a chat. Somehow Mang Ernesto always has time for one more.

npcs.name: Lina
npcs.background: A regular customer stopping to collect a small laundry order.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Rosa always remembers which bundle is mine. That saves me a trip home.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: I was just telling Rosa about my son's school play. He wants to be the narrator.

lines.speaker: Npc
lines.text: Oh, I can come back later. You two look like you're in the middle of something.
